decided: 2026-09-20 by Rohan, before any dense-corpus model was scored
id_to_map_rule: record_arnold.py:322-323 assigns map_ids[episode_id % len(map_ids)], independent of the worker count, so any contiguous id range whose length is a multiple of len(map_ids) is exactly map-balanced
ranges_are: half-open, like a Python slice: "0:6000" is ids 0 to 5999

arenas.note: the Arnold paper's training arenas; maps fixed before any model score was read

arenas_678.note: the Arnold paper's test arenas; no episode of this segment is ever trained on. `ranges.unseen` is the SCORING subset of the unseen-map row, not the whole segment

next_tic_runs.note: the first next-tic runs train on a 2,000-episode prefix of the train range, identical for every backbone

history.what: arenas train 0:6000, val 6000:7000, test 7000:8000 and the next-tic prefixes decided by Rohan before any dense-corpus model was scored
unseen scoring subset declared as arenas_678 ids 0:60 (next_tic_runs.unseen_ids and segments.arenas_678.ranges.unseen)
unseen scoring subset replaced by arenas_678 ids 60:120, before any model was scored on it
history.why: 0:60 is 51 of 60 worker-first episodes (k = 0: ids 0-24 and 26-51; 52-59 are k = 1; 25 has no weapon request and cannot be classified), measured from the raw buttons column with transitions.button_width_report. Only in a recorder process's first episode can Arnold's weapon-select requests execute; val 6000:6100 and test 7000:7100 contain no such episode and training 0:2000 only 32 (1.6%). Scoring on 0:60 would confound map transfer with a control-regime shift. arenas_678 was started three times (RECORDING_LOG.txt: 16, 20, then 16 workers), so k cannot be read off the worker logs there: ids 0-15 were the first 16 workers' first episodes and 16-51 became first episodes again after the restarts. 60:120 holds zero k = 0 episodes (59 with k = 1 to 5, one unclassifiable) and 20 per map. 0:60 may be reported only as a labelled secondary set with its k strata. Source: docs/REVIEW_2026-09-22.md, finding H1.
